items.title: zed-industries/zed
items.summary: Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor built with the Rust language by the developers of Atom and Tree-sitter. It aims to provide a speed-focused experience in software development processes.

snapshot.description: Code at the speed of thought – Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.

items.title: rails/rails
items.summary: Ruby on Rails is a web application framework used for developing database-backed web applications, based on the Model-View-Controller architecture. It aims to standardize processes by providing developers with all the tools they need in one place.

snapshot.description: Ruby on Rails. Rails is a web application framework that includes everything needed to create database-backed web applications according to the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern.

items.title: mpv-player/mpv
items.summary: mpv is a free and open-source media player that runs via the command line. It supports a wide range of media file formats, audio and video codecs, and subtitle types.

snapshot.description: 🎥 Command line media player. mpv is a free (as in freedom) media player for the command line. It supports a wide variety of media file formats, audio and video codecs, and subtitle types.

items.title: react/react
items.summary: React, a JavaScript library for building web and native user interfaces, is designed to simplify interface development processes. This library offers developers the ability to build complex user interfaces in a more organized structure.

snapshot.description: The library for web and native user interfaces. React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces.

items.title: angular/angular
items.summary: Angular is a TypeScript-based framework used for developing web applications. It provides developers with extensive documentation support, from basic concepts to advanced topics, enabling them to deploy applications with confidence.

snapshot.description: Deliver web apps with confidence 🚀. Get started with Angular, learn the fundamentals and explore advanced topics on our documentation website.

items.title: symfony/symfony
items.summary: Symfony is a PHP framework used for developing web and console applications. Offering reusable PHP components, this structure serves as the foundation for many popular web projects.

snapshot.description: The Symfony PHP framework. Symfony is a PHP framework for web and console applications and a set of reusable PHP components. Symfony is used by thousands of web applications and most of the popular PHP projects.

items.title: prometheus/prometheus
items.summary: Prometheus is a monitoring tool that provides system and service monitoring along with time series database management. The system, which collects metrics from targets at specified intervals, evaluates rules to display results and can generate alerts under defined conditions.

snapshot.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database. Prometheus, a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, is a systems and service monitoring system. It collects metrics from configured targets at given intervals, evaluates rule expressions, displays the results, and can trigger alerts when specified conditions are observed.

items.title: microsoft/vscode
items.summary: Visual Studio Code, developed by Microsoft, is an open-source code editor used in software development processes. Developed in collaboration with the community, this platform is written in TypeScript and is available to everyone under the MIT license.

snapshot.description: Visual Studio Code. This repository ("Code - OSS") is where we (Microsoft) develop the Visual Studio Code product together with the community. Not only do we work on code and issues here, but we also publish our roadmap, monthly iteration plans, and our endgame plans. This source code is available to everyone under the standard MIT license.

items.title: nushell/nushell
items.summary: Developed in the Rust language, nushell offers a new command-line interface (shell) that processes data as structured objects. Having reached the minimum-viable-product level, this project is preferred for daily use, although it may show instability in some commands.

snapshot.description: A new type of shell. This project has reached a minimum-viable-product level of quality. Many people use it as their daily driver, but it may be unstable for some commands. Nu's design is subject to change as it matures.

items.title: etcd-io/etcd
items.summary: etcd is a reliable key-value store designed to store critical data in distributed systems. Developed in the Go language, this system focuses on ensuring data consistency within distributed structures.

snapshot.description: Distributed reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system. etcd is a distributed reliable key-value store for the most critical data of a distributed system, with a focus on being:

items.title: openssl/openssl
items.summary: OpenSSL is a general-purpose security library used to encrypt network traffic. It is an open-source software tool that supports Transport Layer Security (TLS), Datagram TLS (DTLS), and QUIC protocols.

snapshot.description: General purpose TLS and crypto library. OpenSSL is a robust, commercial-grade, full-featured Open Source Toolkit for the Transport Layer Security (TLS, formerly SSL), Datagram TLS (DTLS), and QUIC protocols.

items.title: astral-sh/ruff
items.summary: Ruff is a very fast Python linter and formatter developed in the Rust programming language. It is used to improve code quality and accelerate formatting processes in software development.

snapshot.description: An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust. An extremely fast Python linter and code formatter, written in Rust.

items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
items.summary: Tesla plans to end Cybertruck production at its Texas factory in mid-2027 due to low sales figures. The electric pickup truck, which could only find a place in limited markets due to its futuristic design and weight, was positioned as a competitor to traditional pickup models.

snapshot.description: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design.

items.title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost
items.summary: A method that allows a smaller AI model to receive help from Opus on complex tasks offers similar accuracy rates at four times lower cost. This approach aims to increase efficiency by optimizing the use of high-cost models.

items.title: Libghostty 1.0
items.summary: Libghostty 1.0 has been released as a library that allows the core functions of the terminal emulator Ghostty to be integrated into different applications. This version provides a stable interface necessary for developers to incorporate terminal capabilities into their own software.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
items.summary: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, announced by Google, offers higher consistency along with native 15-second video generation and editing capabilities. The model is being made available to developers with 30 percent lower pricing compared to previous versions.

snapshot.description: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings native 15-second video generation and editing, stronger consistency, and 30% lower pricing.

items.title: US FAA says it will phase out floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028
items.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced that it will phase out the floppy disks used in air traffic control systems by 2028. The agency aims to replace this legacy data storage technology with modern digital systems.

items.title: burner22/numbat
items.summary: Numbat, shared on Hugging Face, is an artificial intelligence model checkpoint with 14 trillion parameters and a hybrid architecture. Mentioned in the Claude Code source code, this model represents an intermediate stage of a training process conducted by Anthropic.

snapshot.description: 14T param, 114 layers, hybrid GDN/MLA, MoE (1,224 experts, top-48 + 1 shared), NVFP4. Internal codename numbat, Anthropic's next Mythos-class training run. numbat is the codename referenced in the Claude Code source leak (Mar 2026). This is a checkpoint from that training run, pulled mid-pretraining.

items.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face addresses how large language models (LLMs) process tool outputs. It proposes processing tool data using latent context compression instead of text to reduce distraction and data load in long-term interactions.

snapshot.description: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text

items.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: The article 'Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation' examines the issue of text and vector inconsistency in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods used on offline devices. The study proves that vectors in signed information packets are not compatible with the text and analyzes how this gap can be exploited by attackers.

snapshot.description: Offline retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices is updated through signed knowledge packs that carry text and precomputed embedding vectors. A signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text. We study this text-vector integrity gap. A verifier that recomputes vectors and accepts them within a cosine tolerance concedes a predictable share of queries to an attacker who controls the vectors: the hijack rate equals the distribution of angular retrieval margin

items.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
items.summary: StepX-OPD re-evaluates the multi-teacher on-policy distillation process in text-to-image diffusion models. This method aims to increase the efficiency of few-step sampling stages by combining capabilities such as instruction following and text processing.

snapshot.description: A deployable text-to-image diffusion model must hold several capabilities at once, such as instruction following, text rendering and human preference, and must sample in a few steps. Capabilities and few-step sampling are built in separate stages: a full-step model first consolidates capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation, then serves as a fixed teacher for step distillation. items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: SwarmEvolve is a framework developed to accelerate evolutionary search processes used in solving mathematical and computational problems. By using hundreds of low-cost agents in a swarm, it enables large language models (LLMs) to reason in latent space instead of using text-based thinking processes.

snapshot.description: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. items.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
items.summary: OpenFrontiers, shared by Hugging Face, is an interdisciplinary resource and benchmarking tool prepared to evaluate the scientific research-level problem-solving capabilities of large language models (LLMs). The project offers a structured corpus of unsolved research problems and a test set containing recently solved problems in mathematics.

snapshot.description: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. glossary.explanation: A specialized text editing program used by software developers to write, edit, and manage computer code.
Advanced artificial intelligence models trained on vast amounts of data that can understand human language and generate text.
An architectural structure that ensures software operates systematically by separating its data, the user-facing interface, and its underlying logic.
An infrastructure framework that provides a set of ready-made tools and rules to facilitate software development.
A software tool that compresses audio or video data to reduce its size or decompresses this data for playback.
Applications written in an operating system's native language that run in full compatibility with that system.
A special type of database that records changes over time and stores data in chronological order.
An interface that allows the user to interact with the operating system by entering text-based commands into the computer.
The initial version of a product that contains its core features and is released to gather user feedback.
A simple storage method where data is saved by being paired with a name, allowing it to be quickly retrieved using that name.
A standard protocol that encrypts data to ensure the privacy and security of communication over the internet.
A version of the TLS protocol adapted for faster and more seamless operation, designed to reduce latency in data transmission.
A type of software whose source code is open for anyone to inspect, modify, and enhance.
